name: Bantu-speaking peoples
summary: Hundreds of peoples speaking related Bantu languages, who spread from the area of today’s Cameroon and Nigeria across central, eastern and southern Africa over about 3,000 years, bringing farming and iron working. On the map, this covers the areas not shown as particular kingdoms.

knownFor.label: Iron smelting
knownFor.note: Furnaces for making iron tools and weapons spread with Bantu-speaking farmers.

knownFor.label: Talking drums
knownFor.note: Drums that copy the tones of speech to send messages.

knownFor.label: Ubuntu
knownFor.note: The idea that a person is a person through other people.

location.value: Most of Africa south of the equator, from Cameroon to South Africa and Kenya.
location.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

terrain.value: Rainforest, savannah, highlands and great lakes.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

climate.value: Tropical: wet in the rainforest, with wet and dry seasons on the savannah.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

resources.value: Farmland, iron ore, copper, cattle pasture, ivory.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

disasters.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

population.value: Unknown; grew with the spread of farming.
population.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

urbanisation.value: Mostly villages; later towns and capitals of kingdoms (Mbanza Kongo, Great Zimbabwe).
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

disease.value: Malaria and sleeping sickness limited cattle in some areas.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

migration.value: The Bantu expansion: a long, slow movement of farming peoples east and south, roughly 1500 BCE–500 CE.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

economicBase.value: Farming yams, millet and sorghum; later bananas and cattle; iron tools.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

tradeRoutes.value: Trade in salt, iron, copper and cloth; later links to the Indian Ocean coast (Swahili towns).
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

wealth.value: Wealth in cattle, people and iron.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

moneyAndTax.value: Cowrie shells, copper crosses and cloth as currency in some regions.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

inequality.value: From fairly equal villages to kingdoms with ruling families.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

governmentType.value: Many forms: village councils, chiefdoms and kingdoms (such as Kongo, Luba, Lunda, Buganda, Mutapa).
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

keyRulers.value: Too many to list; see the separate kingdoms (Kongo, Great Zimbabwe, Zulu Kingdom).
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

succession.value: Often through the mother’s or the father’s family line, depending on the people.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

institutions.value: Councils of elders, age groups and kinship.
institutions.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

stability.value: Varied greatly by region and period.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

eliteConflict.value: Disputes between lineages and rival heirs.
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

majorWars.value: Wars between kingdoms; resistance to colonisers in the 19th century.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

territoryChange.value: Spread over about 9 million km² over many centuries.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

alliancesRivals.value: Traded and mixed with hunter-gatherers (Batwa, Khoisan) and with Swahili and Arab traders.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

inventions.value: Iron smelting furnaces, new crops and farming methods for tropical soils.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

scienceEducation.value: Knowledge passed on orally by elders and praise singers.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

openness.value: Adopted new crops (bananas from Asia, maize from the Americas).
openness.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

religion.value: Ancestor spirits and a creator god; later Christianity and Islam.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

languageWriting.value: Over 500 related Bantu languages, including Swahili, Zulu, Xhosa, Shona, Kikongo and Lingala.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

artsArchitecture.value: Sculpture, masks, music and dance; stone towns in Zimbabwe.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

socialStructure.value: Kinship groups and clans; kings and commoners in larger states.
socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

sharedIdentity.value: Shared language family rather than one people.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

neighbours.value: Hunter-gatherers, Nilotic and Cushitic peoples, Swahili and Arab traders, later Europeans.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

ideasReligions.value: Islam on the coast, Christianity in Kongo (1491) and later missions.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

colonisation.value: Colonised by European powers in the late 19th century.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

riseSignals.value: Farming and iron allowed populations to grow and spread.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

peakPeriod.value: No single peak; kingdoms rose and fell in different centuries.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

declineSignals.value: The Atlantic slave trade and colonisation caused great losses.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

outcome.value: Today about 350 million people speak Bantu languages.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

sources.value: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion; Vansina, How Societies Are Born (2004).
sources.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion

overallCertainty.value: Known mostly from linguistics, archaeology and genetics; the timing of the expansion is debated.
overallCertainty.source: Wikipedia: Bantu peoples; Wikipedia: Bantu expansion
